title: Workflows and agents: who owns the control flow

items.stem: Which statement best describes the difference between a workflow and an agent?

options.text: Workflows use tools, while agents answer only from their training
Workflows have no language model inside, while agents always have one
In a workflow, code sets the steps; in an agent, the model sets them
Workflows use small models, while agents always use the largest ones

items.stem: In your makerspace assistant, a Python program always runs check_calendar, then check_training_record, then book_machine, in that order. The model is called inside each step only to fill in the arguments or to write text. Who owns the control flow here?

options.text: The model, because it writes the confirmation message at the end
The program code, because it fixes the order of every step
The model, because it supplies the arguments for each tool
Neither; control flow only exists once a system is an agent

items.stem: Every booking request at the makerspace needs the same three steps in the same order: check the calendar, check the training record, then write the booking. What is the best reason to build this part as a fixed workflow rather than an agent?

options.text: The steps are known in advance, so fixed code is cheaper and more predictable
A fixed workflow can recover from surprises that an agent cannot handle
An agent cannot call tools, so a workflow is the only way to book
Fixed workflows give more accurate answers on every kind of task

items.stem: For one request, a fixed workflow in your assistant always makes exactly 2 model calls: one to classify the question and one to write the answer. An agent handling the same request requests 4 tools, one per model call, and then writes its final answer in one more call. Each model call costs the same. How many more model calls does the agent use than the workflow?
In one or two sentences: in a workflow, what decides which step runs next, and in an agent, what decides?
Which makerspace task is the best candidate for an agent rather than a fixed workflow?

options.text: Sending the same reminder text to each student the day before a booking
Booking a slot once the student has confirmed machine, day and time
Replying to a student who asks for the shop's opening hours
Helping a student whose print keeps failing, with unknown lookups needed
